title: Drivers line up as fuel price falls below $1 in northwest Winnipeg before increasing
summary: Drivers were lining up Tuesday morning at one gas station for prices not seen in Winnipeg in a long time. The Domo station in the Northgate Shopping Centre parking lot on McPhillips Street was…

image.caption: Cars line up for low gas prices at Domo in the Northgate Shopping Centre parking lot in Winnipeg on Tuesday morning. (Meaghan Ketcheson/CBC)

blocks.text: Manitoba·Updated

Drivers were lining up Tuesday morning at one gas station for prices not seen in Winnipeg in a long time. The Domo station in the Northgate Shopping Centre parking lot on McPhillips Street was selling regular gas at 97.9 cents per litre.
Average price in city is 134.9, but Domo on McPhillips Street had it at 97.9
Winnipeg drivers were lining up Tuesday morning at one gas station for prices not seen in the city in a long time.
The Domo station in the Northgate Shopping Centre parking lot on McPhillips Street was selling regular gas at 97.9 cents per litre.

"It's awesome," said Cathy Knowles, who was with one of about two dozen vehicles lined up. "Everyone's worried about the gas 'cause everything's going up, so this is a good deal. So, let's take advantage of it now."
She went by the Domo on Monday night just after the prices first dropped, but the line was too long. So, she waited until early Tuesday before going back.
"I couldn't believe it. I was flabbergasted, actually," Knowles said. "I was hoping to get a little bit closer [this morning], but oh well. It is what it is."
A Petro-Canada station nearby was selling for 113.9, and many other stations had it at 117.9, according to price tracking company GasBuddy.
However, there are still some stations with prices as high as 149.9.
Some drivers took advantage of the cheap price to fill fuel containers, in addition to their vehicles. (Travis Golby/CBC)
By the afternoon, the price at the McPhillips Domo had increased to 113.9.

But it's still a better price than many other locations in the city, where the average regular fuel price is currently 134.9, according to GasBuddy. And that's down from an average of 171.5 in September.
The last time prices were at 97 cents on average was August 2020. Some stations briefly dipped to that price in February this year, but as a whole, the average price was a lot lower, too, at 123.3.
In Canada, the average price right now is 148.6.
3 main reasons for lower prices
There are three primary reasons contributing to the lower prices, according to Shiu-Yik Au, an associate professor of finance at the University of Manitoba.

One is the Democrats winning the midterm elections in the United States. The market is predicting that will lead to some type of negotiated settlements regarding the Iran war and open the Strait of Hormuz, enabling oil tankers to pass unimpeded, he said.
The second reason is the annual shift in fuel from a summer blend to winter blend.
"In summertime, there are different requirements than in wintertime," Au said.

Winter gas contains butane, a relatively cheap additive that helps cars start faster and run better in colder weather. In the summer, butane is left out in favour of alkylates, which burn cleaner but are more expensive to produce.

"The final [reason] is that there's less demand. We all love to go on summer road trips — the November road trip, December road trip, not as exciting," Au said. "Because there's less demand, the cost is going down."

blocks.text: Those savings on gas have a ripple effect on the broader economy, he said.
"This is giving us a little bit of breathing room just in time for the Christmas shopping season. And so hopefully, that will help us stimulate things."
The ongoing variation in prices across different stations is a bit unusual, Au said, though he did say the price below $1 is less than the current wholesale cost for Domo.
"So, these people are losing money on their gasoline," he said. "I suspect it's more of a fun kind of price war … let's see how low we can go, and have some fun with it."
